benchmark.category: a voice-ordered fireworks shot-kit app with a moderated crew video wall
benchmark.users: TikTok dancers and their crews in Phnom Penh ordering fireworks for a 15-second dance shot and showing the resulting clips off on a crew wall

requirements.source_phrase: Safer Big Uploads: Stop huge videos before they upload so one crew can't slow the wall for everyone
requirements.statement: POST /api/clips refuses an empty body, a missing crew_name, a non-video content type and a body larger than the configured limit (61 MB or more) with a 4xx whose body says which limit was broken — the oversize case answered 413 before the whole body is buffered to disk or memory — and leaves no clip row and no stored blob behind.
requirements.notes: Features list requires 413 for an upload over 61 MB, and the agent's own open item said the size limit was checked only after the whole file had arrived; early rejection is the server half of 'before they upload'. Measure the response and the leftover blobs/disk use, and confirm the app still answers other requests meanwhile.

requirements.source_phrase: Fresh Weekly Winner: Pick Clip of the Week only from clips posted this week, with a fallback banner when nobody has likes yet
requirements.statement: GET /api/clips returns only approved, non-deleted clips, each with id, crew_name, kit_id (empty when none), posted time and week_likes, sorted by week_likes descending then newest first, plus top_crews with each crew's week like total highest first and a featured pair clip_of_week plus featured_kind: when an approved non-deleted clip posted within the last 7 days has at least one like in that window, clip_of_week is the one with the highest week_likes (ties by newest posted) and featured_kind is 'winner'; when no clip posted within the last 7 days has a like, clip_of_week is the newest approved non-deleted clip posted within the last 7 days and featured_kind is 'fresh'; otherwise clip_of_week is null and featured_kind is 'none'; an approved clip posted more than 7 days ago is never featured whatever its likes, and an empty store returns empty arrays with clip_of_week null.
requirements.notes: Features list requires featured_kind and clip_of_week to follow the winner/fresh/none rules with older-than-7-days clips never featured; the user's answer adds the fresh fallback as the newest clip. Assumption recorded: 'this week' is the same rolling last-seven-days window week_likes uses (R-282), not a calendar week — if the app uses a calendar week the same boundary must apply to both. Probe the boundary with a clip posted 8 days ago holding more likes than one posted 2 days ago.

requirements.source_phrase: Fresh Weekly Winner: Pick Clip of the Week only from clips posted this week, with a fallback banner when nobody has likes yet
requirements.statement: At the top of the Crew Video Wall a clip-of-week banner (data-testid clip-of-week-banner) renders the clip GET /api/clips features: with a winner it shows the label 'Clip of the week', the crew name, the stored like count, a like control, an open-kit link when the clip has a kit and a share control (data-testid clip-of-week-share-btn); with a fresh clip and no likes yet it shows the label 'Fresh drop' together with the 'Be this week's winner' prompt (data-testid clip-of-week-be-winner), the newest clip's crew name and a like control, and no share control until it has a like; liking the fresh clip once flips the banner to the 'Clip of the week' label and reveals the share control; when no clip qualifies the banner shows the prompt with no clip and no share control, never a blank card or a broken image.
requirements.notes: Features list expects the label 'Fresh drop' plus be-winner text when there are no likes and a flip to 'Clip of the week' with clip-of-week-share-btn after a like; both fallback options in the answer (newest clip as 'Fresh drop' and the 'Be this week's winner' prompt) appear together. The none state is an assumption: with no clip posted this week nothing is featured, so only the prompt shows.

requirements.source_phrase: Let uploaders pick one of their kits
requirements.statement: The real-shoot upload panel offers a kit selector (data-testid upload-shoot-kit-select) listing every kit built or opened on this device, newest first, rather than only the 10 most recent, marks the chosen kit, and sends its kit_id with the upload; a clip posted from a preview recording carries its kit_id automatically even when no kit is picked, and a clip stored with no kit_id shows no Open this Shot Kit link.
requirements.notes: The user's rule is that uploaders pick one of their kits; the build report below the marker says the dropdown offers only the 10 most recently built or opened kits, so the requirement is written for every kit the device holds and Phase 4 checks the cap.

requirements.source_phrase: Go Live Update: Redeploy so the live app gets the admin lock, progress bar and Clip of the Week
requirements.statement: The live deployment serves the same build as the preview: on the live app's URL the home page shows the upload progress bar with the longer-than-one-minute warning, the Crew Video Wall shows the Clip of the Week banner, an approved clip shows an Open this Shot Kit link, and /admin grants clip review only to swarnimsandeep@yahoo.com, so no feature verified in preview is missing on the live app.
requirements.notes: The user asked for a redeploy so the live app receives the earlier upgrades; the build summary states the latest changes are preview-only and a production deployment exists separately. Test by driving the live origin's page and API, not by comparing commit hashes; if the live origin is unreachable from the test environment, report parity as unverified with the reason rather than passed.

requirements.source_phrase: Winner Share Card: Make a shareable Telegram card for the Clip of the Week crew with their kit link
requirements.statement: On the Clip of the Week banner a share control (data-testid clip-of-week-share-btn) is visible once a winning clip exists, and activating it prepares both a picture card and a text message, each carrying the kit link of the winning crew's clip, without navigating away from the wall.
requirements.notes: The user's answer chose both 'Picture card + link' and 'Text message + link', so offering only one form is a missing feature; the features list names clip-of-week-share-btn and expects the control absent when there is no winner.

requirements.source_phrase: Winner Share Card: Make a shareable Telegram card for the Clip of the Week crew with their kit link
requirements.statement: The shared winner artifact is a decodable PNG of at least 500x500 pixels and non-trivial file size whose drawn content names the winning crew, marks the clip as the Clip of the Week for BoomDrop and shows the crew's kit link legibly, the download is named boomdrop-winner.png with a PNG content type, and the accompanying Telegram text message names the crew and carries the full kit URL.
requirements.notes: Files/media class: word the check by the content of the file — decode the PNG, read the drawn text for the crew name and the kit URL, check dimensions and byte length — never by the status of the download response; a blank, cropped or placeholder card fails.

requirements.source_phrase: Winner Share Card: Make a shareable Telegram card for the Clip of the Week crew with their kit link
requirements.statement: The kit link placed in the winner card and the Telegram share is built from the featured clip's stored kit_id, and GET /api/shot-kit/{that id} returns that crew's stored kit whose name, cues and totals are what /?kit=<id> renders; a featured clip with no kit_id yields a card and text with no link rather than the string 'undefined' or another clip's kit.
requirements.notes: The link must open the winning crew's kit; the features list checks the Telegram share URL contains the kit link, so assert the id in the URL equals clip_of_week.kit_id and that R-175 returns that kit from a fresh session.

requirements.source_phrase: Safer Big Uploads: Stop huge videos before they upload so one crew can't slow the wall for everyone
requirements.statement: Choosing a shoot video larger than the 60 MB limit in the upload panel shows a readable 'file is too large' message in the selected language and starts no upload — no request leaves the browser, no progress bar appears, and the upload control stays usable so the user can pick a smaller clip.
requirements.notes: 'Stop huge videos before they upload' is a client-side pre-check; verify by network observation that an over-limit file produces zero upload requests, since a passing server 413 alone would mean the big file was still sent.

requirements.source_phrase: Safer Big Uploads: Stop huge videos before they upload so one crew can't slow the wall for everyone
requirements.statement: While one upload from a client is still being received or transcoded, a second upload submitted in parallel from the same client is answered 429 with a readable reason and stores no clip, and the server transcodes at most two videos at a time, so GET /api/clips and other visitors' pages stay responsive while a large upload is in flight.
requirements.notes: Features list expects 429 for a parallel upload from the same client and the agent's fix states at most 2 videos are processed at once; submit three concurrent uploads from different device ids and watch the third wait rather than transcode alongside the first two, measuring GET /api/clips latency throughout.

requirements.statement: Opening /admin as swarnimsandeep@yahoo.com shows a 'Live on the wall' tab beside the pending review queue; the tab lists the clips currently approved on the wall, each with a remove control, and activating remove takes that clip off the wall once the list refreshes.
requirements.notes: Build reveal below the marker: the admin page now has a 'Live on the wall' tab so an approved-by-mistake clip can be removed; derived from the user's approval step plus that reveal.

requirements.statement: Removing an approved clip as swarnimsandeep@yahoo.com marks it removed so GET /api/clips no longer lists it and GET /api/clips/{id}/video returns 404, while the same request from a signed-out caller, a member account or any account other than swarnimsandeep@yahoo.com is refused with 401 or 403 and leaves the clip on the wall.
requirements.notes: Paranoid privacy half of a removal control: hiding the button is not enough, the removal must be admin-only on the server and persisted (the existing is_deleted rule, R-234), not a browser-side filter.

requirements.statement: While an upload started from the longer-than-one-minute warning is in flight the warning's 'post the first minute', 'post the full video' and cancel actions are disabled, and a second press or double click posts exactly one clip, so the pending queue gains one row and the 'Sent for review' toast appears once.
requirements.notes: Agent fix below the marker: pressing the warning buttons twice can no longer post the same video twice; check the queue count and the toast count, not the click.

requirements.statement: After a like from the Clip of the Week banner or from a wall tile, the banner's featured clip, its label and the affected like counts update from the server's response in the same view without a manual page reload, the liked control stays filled, and the wall's top-crews ordering reflects the new count.
requirements.notes: Agent fix: 'The banner and like counts refresh after a like'; features list requires the banner to flip from 'Fresh drop' to 'Clip of the week' after a like, which only works if the client refetches the featured payload rather than patching local state.

requirements.statement: The like count the banner shows for the featured clip equals that clip's week_likes as GET /api/clips returns it, and the featured clip's id equals the id of the top-ranked approved clip of the last seven days, so the banner never shows a count or a clip the wall listing disagrees with.
requirements.notes: A displayed value must equal the stored value it is labelled as; seed a known like count on the featured clip and compare the banner, the tile and the API payload.

requirements.statement: When the featured clip's video fails to load or decode, the banner shows a readable error in the selected language together with the crew name and keeps its like, open-kit and share controls usable, never a blank or permanently black player.
requirements.notes: Agent open item: 'A broken featured video shows a blank player instead of an error message'; the wall tiles already owe the same per-tile error (R-261), so the banner must match.

requirements.statement: When the browser cannot read the chosen video's duration, the upload panel does not post the full video silently: an over-60-second clip still reaches the user as the three-choice warning (for example by reading the duration server-side before posting), while an unreadable short clip uploads normally with the progress bar.
requirements.notes: Agent open item: 'If a phone can't read a video's length, the warning is skipped and the full video is posted.' The user asked for a clear warning above one minute, so a silent full-length post is a mismatch; simulate with a media file whose metadata the browser cannot parse.

requirements.statement: When the server refuses an upload, the panel shows the server's reason as a toast in the selected language — a too-large message for 413 and an already-uploading message for 429 — resets the progress bar to idle, re-enables the upload control, and never shows the 'Sent for review' confirmation.
requirements.notes: Features list: '413 ... normal upload still works and UI shows server error message in a toast'. Nothing may fail silently and nothing may report a success the server refused; also confirm a normal upload still succeeds after the error.

requirements.statement: Pressing the winner share control once downloads exactly one boomdrop-winner.png and opens exactly one Telegram share tab, a second press while the first is still preparing stacks no second download or tab, and the toast names what happened.
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of the share action: a control acts once and answers on screen; a duplicated download or an extra share tab per double press is the usual defect.

requirements.statement: In a desktop browser without file sharing the winner share downloads boomdrop-winner.png and opens a real https://t.me/share/url link in a new tab whose url parameter percent-encodes the crew's kit URL and whose text parameter names the crew and the Clip of the Week, with Web Share file support handing the picture plus link to the platform sheet instead; no key or token appears in the URL and the app page and its banner stay unchanged.
requirements.notes: Features list names exactly this fallback (download plus Telegram URL containing the kit link plus toast); third-party integration class worded as a real outbound share URL through the app's own code path rather than a stubbed intent.

requirements.statement: At 390x844 and at 1280x800 the clip-of-week banner renders above the wall grid without overlapping it, and its label, crew name, like count, like control, open-kit link and share control all render without clipping or page-level horizontal overflow in both the 'Clip of the week' and the 'Fresh drop' states, with the share toast visible.
requirements.notes: Layout class at the product's two test widths; the banner is the topmost block on the wall, so overflow there pushes the whole wall sideways on a phone.

requirements.statement: While a 60 MB video uploads the progress bar keeps advancing and the page stays responsive — the wall list, the banner and the mic can still be used with no long main-thread stall — and closing the panel or leaving the page stops the upload with no clip stored.
requirements.notes: Performance and resource-leak class: 'one crew can't slow the wall for everyone' also applies to the uploader's own page, and an aborted upload must leave nothing half-written.

requirements.statement: The home page and /admin load with every bundle and asset the winner share card renderer, the fresh banner and the upload size check reference returning 200 with the right content type, and the sequence open the wall, like a clip, share the winner, upload a short video raises no uncaught console error and no failed asset request.
requirements.notes: Build/deployment class for the newly added chunks; a missing share-card module surfaces only when the share button is pressed, so run the whole sequence.

requirements.statement: After the winner share, fresh-winner and big-upload changes a short shoot video still uploads with a working progress bar and 'Sent for review' toast, a video longer than one minute still shows the three-choice warning, an approved clip with a kit still shows an 'Open this Shot Kit' link that opens that kit, and admin+clerk_test@boomdrop.dev still gets no review access while swarnimsandeep@yahoo.com can review.
requirements.notes: Features list names this regression explicitly ('Regression: upload progress bar, long video warning, kit link, admin lock from iteration 8'); run it at 390x844 and at 1280x800.
